name: Kitchen Appliances
tagline: Built-in equipment that has to be planned, not bought later
description: Appliances drive the kitchen layout: a built-in oven needs a housing and a 16 A point, a dishwasher needs inlet, outlet and a level floor. Every entry here lists the cut-out, the service and the clearance so the carpentry and the electrical drawings agree.

materials.name: Chimney
materials.blurb: Extraction over the hob — sized by kitchen volume, not looks
materials.description: Indian cooking needs real extraction: 1200 m³/h and up for a regularly used hob. Ducted always beats recirculating, and the duct run should be short, straight and rise as it goes.

materials.name: Hob
materials.blurb: Gas, induction or hybrid cooktop set into the counter
materials.description: Cut-out size and gas point position must reach the carpenter before the counter is templated. Leave 50 mm clearance behind for the gas connection and 300 mm of landing space on each side.

materials.name: Built-in oven
materials.blurb: Housed at eye level or under the counter, with its own circuit
materials.description: Needs a dedicated 16 A point, ventilation gaps around the housing, and a cabinet built to the exact aperture. Eye-level installation is safer and far more comfortable to use.

materials.name: Built-in microwave
materials.blurb: Integrated into the tall unit so the counter stays clear
materials.description: A trim kit lets a microwave sit flush in joinery. Confirm the ventilation clearance and put the point inside the housing, not behind the appliance where a plug will not fit.

materials.name: Dishwasher
materials.blurb: Freestanding or integrated — needs inlet, outlet and a level base
materials.description: Increasingly standard in Indian kitchens. Plan a hot or cold inlet, a waste connection above trap level, and a 16 A point; an integrated model also needs a matching shutter and a level plinth.

materials.name: Refrigerator
materials.blurb: Freestanding or built-in, with ventilation the joinery must allow
materials.description: The biggest single appliance decision. Built-in and side-by-side models need generous rear and top ventilation plus door-swing clearance — check the plan against the fully open door, not the closed one.

materials.name: Wine cooler
materials.blurb: Temperature-controlled wine storage, freestanding or built-in
materials.description: Single or dual zone, sized in bottles. Built-in units vent from the front, so they can sit under a counter; freestanding ones cannot, and will overheat if boxed in.

materials.name: Built-in coffee machine
materials.blurb: Plumbed or tank-fed machine integrated into the tall unit
materials.description: A hospitality touch that needs a 16 A point, a housing aperture and — for plumbed models — a water line. Decide plumbed versus tank before the joinery is cut.

materials.name: Water purifier
materials.blurb: RO or UV unit under the sink or on the wall
materials.description: Under-sink installation keeps the counter clear but needs a dedicated tap, a drain connection for the reject line and space for filter changes. Plan the service access, not just the unit.
